result.question: I'm worried the paper insulation in Transformer 1 at MAIN may be involved. Pull co and co2 for every sample in the available window and work out the CO2/CO ratio for each sample. Flag any sample with a ratio below 3, which suggests paper involved in a fault, or above 10, which suggests general cellulose ageing. Also give me the min, max and mean of co and co2 over the window. Tell me whether the ratio is trending up or down across the samples. If co2 is missing for a sample, skip the ratio for that sample and say so. If co2 has no data at all, report the co trend alongside oxygen instead and say that the ratio test couldn't be done.
result.answer:
Nothing further is needed — co and co2 are both fully populated for all 5 samples, so I have everything to compute the ratios and trends. Here's the analysis.

## Transformer 1 (MAIN) — CO₂/CO ratio, 2024-01-15 → 2024-01-19 (5 daily samples)

| Timestamp | CO (ppm) | CO₂ (ppm) | CO₂/CO | Flag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-01-15 | 32 | 1344 | 42.00 | ⚠ >10 — general cellulose ageing |
| 2024-01-16 | 30 | 1300 | 43.33 | ⚠ >10 — general cellulose ageing |
| 2024-01-17 | 35 | 1350 | 38.57 | ⚠ >10 — general cellulose ageing |
| 2024-01-18 | 33 | 1325 | 40.15 | ⚠ >10 — general cellulose ageing |
| 2024-01-19 | 32 | 1340 | 41.88 | ⚠ >10 — general cellulose ageing |

- **No samples with ratio < 3** — no signature of paper directly involved in an active fault.
- **All 5 samples have ratio > 10** (range 38.6–43.3), consistent with general/normal cellulose ageing rather than a paper-involved hot spot.
- **No samples skipped** — co2 was present for every sample, so the ratio was computed for all 5.

## Summary statistics over the window

| Gas | Min | Max | Mean |
|---|---|---|---|
| CO | 30 | 35 | 32.4 ppm |
| CO₂ | 1300 | 1350 | 1331.8 ppm |

## Ratio trend

Sequence: 42.0 → 43.3 → 38.6 → 40.2 → 41.9. A linear fit gives a slope of about **−0.34 per sample**, so the ratio is **slightly trending down** across the window (first-to-last drop of ~0.1; mean 41.2), but the movement is small and oscillatory — practically flat. The dip on 01-17 coincides with the CO peak (35 ppm), which is the one day worth noting; it recovered the next day.

## Interpretation

Absolute CO (~32 ppm) and CO₂ (~1330 ppm) are both low and stable — nothing here suggests accelerated paper degradation. The consistently high ratio (~40) points to slow, ordinary cellulose ageing rather than an active fault involving the insulation. If you want, I can cross-check this against the hydrocarbon gases via the Rogers Ratio DGA interpreter, or run the health-index model using the full oil-quality set (water content, dielectric rigidity, interfacial tension, DBDS) that's also available on this asset.
